items.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012
items.q: the list of members is like John B. Mellon, George D. Rockefeller, blah-blah, Benny Goodman.

ctx.x: And Benny playing the Weber Clarinet Concerto, with seven thousand people waiting to hear “Honeysuckle Rose.” It was incredible. So after we finished that night he said, “Let’s go and get something to eat.” So I said, “Okay.” So we went off to get something to eat and I was having some apple pie. So he reached over and he said, “Let me try a piece of that.” So he took — “oh that’s good,” he said, “oh by the way this is for you.” And it was a jewelry box. I said, “What’s this for, Benny?” He said, “That’s for your…

paying Zoot Sims.” I said, “Good.” It was a hundred dollars more. So then he said, “Let’s go out to eat and celebrate.” So he took me to, I think it’s called the Century Club. It’s on Fifth Avenue. And the list of members is like John B. Mellon, George D. Rockefeller, blah-blah, Benny Goodman. So we get there and oh it’s incredible. He said, “Do you like it?” I said, “Oh, Benny, it’s just incredible.” It’s all beautiful paneled you know. He said, “It’s like a movie, isn’t it?” I said, “Yeah.” So the waiter came…
Right. I’ll take that in my salary.
